Can a corrupt throne be Your ally —

differences.authoritative: Can a corrupt throne be Your ally—one devising mischief by decree?

before the LORD,

differences.authoritative: Make a joyful noise to the LORD, all the earth; break forth—let your cry ring out, and sing praises!

differences.authoritative: Let them praise Your great and awesome name—He is holy!

differences.authoritative: You will rise up and have compassion on Zion, for it is time to show her favor—the appointed time has come.

differences.authoritative: As for man, his days are like grass—he blooms like a flower of the field;

differences.authoritative: But from everlasting to everlasting the loving devotion of the LORD extends to those who fear Him, and His righteousness to their children’s children—

the mountains rose and the valleys sank

He sent a man before them—
Joseph, sold as a slave.
differences.authoritative: He sent a man before them—Joseph, sold as a slave.

differences.authoritative: He sent darkness, and it became dark—yet they defied His words.

differences.structured:

gnats throughout their country.
differences.authoritative: He spoke, and insects swarmed—gnats throughout their country.

differences.structured:

differences.structured:

differences.structured:
Light dawns in the darkness for the upright —

differences.authoritative: Light dawns in the darkness for the upright—for the gracious, compassionate, and righteous.

differences.structured:
He will bless those who fear the LORD—

differences.authoritative: He will bless those who fear the LORD—small and great alike.

differences.structured:
I love the LORD, for He has heard my voice —
my appeal for mercy.
differences.authoritative: I love the LORD, for He has heard my voice—my appeal for mercy.

differences.structured:
You rebuke the arrogant —
the cursed who stray from Your commandments.
differences.authoritative: You rebuke the arrogant—the cursed who stray from Your commandments.

differences.structured:
All Your commandments are faithful;
I am persecuted without cause— help me!
differences.authoritative: All Your commandments are faithful; I am persecuted without cause—help me!

differences.structured:
How sweet are Your words to my taste—
sweeter than honey in my mouth!
differences.authoritative: How sweet are Your words to my taste—sweeter than honey in my mouth!

differences.structured:
A song of ascents. Of David.

If the LORD had not been on our side—
let Israel now declare—
differences.authoritative: A song of ascents. Of David. If the LORD had not been on our side—let Israel now declare—

differences.structured:
In vain you rise early
and stay up late,
toiling for bread to eat —
for He gives sleep to His beloved.
differences.authoritative: In vain you rise early and stay up late, toiling for bread to eat—for He gives sleep to His beloved.

differences.structured:
A song of ascents.

Many a time they have persecuted me from my youth—
let Israel now declare—
differences.authoritative: A song of ascents. Many a time they have persecuted me from my youth—let Israel now declare—

differences.structured:
My soul waits for the Lord
more than watchmen wait for the morning—
more than watchmen wait for the morning.
differences.authoritative: My soul waits for the Lord more than watchmen wait for the morning—more than watchmen wait for the morning.

differences.structured:
Blessed be the LORD from Zion —
He who dwells in Jerusalem.

Hallelujah!
differences.authoritative: Blessed be the LORD from Zion—He who dwells in Jerusalem. Hallelujah!

differences.structured:
He made the great lights —

differences.structured:
and slaughtered mighty kings—
His loving devotion endures forever.

differences.authoritative: and Og king of Bashan—His loving devotion endures forever.

a perpetual wasteland.

the remainder of My nation will dispossess them.”

He is the King of Glory.
Selah

differences.authoritative: Jacob fled to the land of Aram and Israel worked for a wife—for a wife he tended sheep.

differences.structured:
You are destroyed, O Israel,
because you are against Me —
against your helper.
differences.authoritative: You are destroyed, O Israel, because you are against Me—against your helper.

differences.structured:
Although he flourishes among his brothers,
an east wind will come —
a wind from the LORD
rising up from the desert.
His fountain will fail,
and his spring will run dry.
The wind will plunder his treasury
of every precious article.
differences.authoritative: Although he flourishes among his brothers, an east wind will come—a wind from the LORD rising up from the desert. His fountain will fail, and his spring will run dry. The wind will plunder his treasury of every precious article.

differences.structured:
The grapevine is dried up,
and the fig tree is withered;
the pomegranate, palm, and apple—
all the trees of the orchard— are withered.
Surely the joy of mankind has dried up.
differences.authoritative: The grapevine is dried up, and the fig tree is withered; the pomegranate, palm, and apple—all the trees of the orchard—are withered. Surely the joy of mankind has dried up.

differences.structured:
Has not the food been cut off
before our very eyes —
joy and gladness
from the house of our God?
differences.authoritative: Has not the food been cut off before our very eyes—joy and gladness from the house of our God?

differences.structured:
Before them a fire devours,
and behind them a flame scorches.
The land before them is like the Garden of Eden,
but behind them, it is like a desert wasteland —
surely nothing will escape them.
differences.authoritative: Before them a fire devours, and behind them a flame scorches. The land before them is like the Garden of Eden, but behind them, it is like a desert wasteland—surely nothing will escape them.

differences.structured:
Who knows? He may turn and relent
and leave a blessing behind Him —
grain and drink offerings
for the LORD your God.
differences.authoritative: Who knows? He may turn and relent and leave a blessing behind Him—grain and drink offerings for the LORD your God.

differences.structured:
I will repay you for the years eaten by locusts —
the swarming locust, the young locust,
the destroying locust, and the devouring locust—
My great army that I sent against you.
differences.authoritative: I will repay you for the years eaten by locusts—the swarming locust, the young locust, the destroying locust, and the devouring locust—My great army that I sent against you.

differences.structured:
And everyone who calls on the name of the LORD
will be saved;
for on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem
there will be deliverance, as the LORD has promised,
among the remnant called by the LORD.’’
differences.authoritative: And everyone who calls on the name of the LORD will be saved; for on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there will be deliverance, as the LORD has promised, among the remnant called by the LORD.
differences.engineeringDecision: extra closing-quote string in USJ; retain TXT

differences.structured:
I will sell your sons and daughters into the hands of the people of Judah, and they will sell them to the Sabeans — to a distant nation.”
Indeed, the LORD has spoken.
differences.authoritative: I will sell your sons and daughters into the hands of the people of Judah, and they will sell them to the Sabeans—to a distant nation.” Indeed, the LORD has spoken.

differences.structured: These are the words of Amos, who was among the sheepherders of Tekoa— what he saw concerning Israel two years before the earthquake, in the days when Uzziah was king of Judah and Jeroboam son of Jehoashwas king of Israel.
differences.authoritative: These are the words of Amos, who was among the sheepherders of Tekoa—what he saw concerning Israel two years before the earthquake, in the days when Uzziah was king of Judah and Jeroboam son of Jehoash was king of Israel.

differences.structured:
Their king will go into exile —
he and his princes together,”
says the LORD.
differences.authoritative: Their king will go into exile—he and his princes together,” says the LORD.

differences.structured:
The lion has roared —
who will not fear?
The Lord GOD has spoken —
who will not prophesy?
differences.authoritative: The lion has roared—who will not fear? The Lord GOD has spoken—who will not prophesy?

differences.structured:
For behold, He who forms the mountains,
who creates the wind
and reveals His thoughts to man,
who turns the dawn to darkness
and strides on the heights of the earth—
the LORD, the God of Hosts, is His name.”
differences.authoritative: For behold, He who forms the mountains, who creates the wind and reveals His thoughts to man, who turns the dawn to darkness and strides on the heights of the earth—the LORD, the God of Hosts, is His name.”

differences.structured:
He who made the Pleiades and Orion,
who turns darkness into dawn
and darkens day into night,
who summons the waters of the sea
and pours them over the face of the earth —
the LORD is His name —
differences.authoritative: He who made the Pleiades and Orion, who turns darkness into dawn and darkens day into night, who summons the waters of the sea and pours them over the face of the earth—the LORD is His name—

differences.structured:
The Lord GOD has sworn by Himself— the LORD, the God of Hosts, has declared:

“I abhor Jacob’s pride
and detest his citadels,
so I will deliver up the city
and everything in it.”
differences.authoritative: The Lord GOD has sworn by Himself—the LORD, the God of Hosts, has declared: “I abhor Jacob’s pride and detest his citadels, so I will deliver up the city and everything in it.”

differences.structured:
Behold, the days are coming,
declares the Lord GOD,
when I will send a famine on the land —
not a famine of bread or a thirst for water,
but a famine of hearing the words of the LORD.
differences.authoritative: Behold, the days are coming, declares the Lord GOD, when I will send a famine on the land—not a famine of bread or a thirst for water, but a famine of hearing the words of the LORD.

differences.structured:
In that day the lovely young women —
the young men as well —
will faint from thirst.
differences.authoritative: In that day the lovely young women—the young men as well—will faint from thirst.

differences.structured:
Those who swear by the guilt of Samaria
and say, ‘As surely as your god lives, O Dan,’
or, ‘As surely as the way of Beersheba lives’—
they will fall, never to rise again.”
differences.authoritative: Those who swear by the guilt of Samaria and say, ‘As surely as your god lives, O Dan,’ or, ‘As surely as the way of Beersheba lives’—they will fall, never to rise again.”

differences.structured:
The Lord GOD of Hosts,
He who touches the earth and it melts,
and all its dwellers mourn —
all the land rises like the Nile,
then sinks like the river of Egypt —
differences.authoritative: The Lord GOD of Hosts, He who touches the earth and it melts, and all its dwellers mourn—all the land rises like the Nile, then sinks like the river of Egypt—

differences.structured:
All the sinners among My people
will die by the sword —
all those who say,
‘Disaster will never draw near or confront us.’”
differences.authoritative: All the sinners among My people will die by the sword—all those who say, ‘Disaster will never draw near or confront us.’”

differences.structured:
This is the vision of Obadiah:

This is what the Lord GOD says about Edom —

We have heard a message from the LORD;
an envoy has been sent among the nations
to say, “Rise up,
and let us go to battle against her!”—
differences.authoritative: This is the vision of Obadiah: This is what the Lord GOD says about Edom—We have heard a message from the LORD; an envoy has been sent among the nations to say, “Rise up, and let us go to battle against her!”—

differences.structured:
“If thieves came to you,
if robbers by night —
oh, how you will be ruined —
would they not steal only what they wanted?
If grape gatherers came to you,
would they not leave some gleanings?
differences.authoritative: “If thieves came to you, if robbers by night—oh, how you will be ruined—would they not steal only what they wanted? If grape gatherers came to you, would they not leave some gleanings?

differences.structured:
Then the house of Jacob will be a blazing fire,
and the house of Joseph a burning flame;
but the house of Esau will be stubble —
Jacob will set it ablaze and consume it.
Therefore no survivor will remain
from the house of Esau.”
For the LORD has spoken.
differences.authoritative: Then the house of Jacob will be a blazing fire, and the house of Joseph a burning flame; but the house of Esau will be stubble—Jacob will set it ablaze and consume it. Therefore no survivor will remain from the house of Esau.” For the LORD has spoken.

differences.structured:
Those from the Negev will possess the mountains of Esau;
those from the foothillswill possess the land of the Philistines.
They will occupy the fields of Ephraim and Samaria,
and Benjamin will possess Gilead.
differences.authoritative: Those from the Negev will possess the mountains of Esau; those from the foothills will possess the land of the Philistines. They will occupy the fields of Ephraim and Samaria, and Benjamin will possess Gilead.

differences.structured:
This time Jonah got up and went to Nineveh, in accordance with the word of the LORD.
Now Nineveh was an exceedingly great city,requiring a three-day journey.
differences.authoritative: This time Jonah got up and went to Nineveh, in accordance with the word of the LORD. Now Nineveh was an exceedingly great city, requiring a three-day journey.

differences.structured: When God saw their actions— that they had turned from their evil ways— He relented from the disaster He had threatened to bring upon them.
differences.authoritative: When God saw their actions—that they had turned from their evil ways—He relented from the disaster He had threatened to bring upon them.

differences.structured: So he prayed to the LORD, saying, “O LORD, is this not what I said while I was still in my own country? This is why I was so quick to flee toward Tarshish. I knew that You are a gracious and compassionate God, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion — One who relents from sending disaster.
differences.authoritative: So he prayed to the LORD, saying, “O LORD, is this not what I said while I was still in my own country? This is why I was so quick to flee toward Tarshish. I knew that You are a gracious and compassionate God, slow to anger, abounding in loving devotion—One who relents from sending disaster.

differences.structured: This is the word of the LORD that came to Micah the Moreshite in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah — what he saw regarding Samaria and Jerusalem:
differences.authoritative: This is the word of the LORD that came to Micah the Moreshite in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah—what he saw regarding Samaria and Jerusalem:
Therefore, send farewell gifts to Moresheth-gath; the houses of Achzib will prove deceptive to the kings of Israel.

differences.structured:
Arise and depart,
for this is not your place of rest,
because its defilement brings destruction—
a grievous destruction!
differences.authoritative: Arise and depart, for this is not your place of rest, because its defilement brings destruction—a grievous destruction!

differences.structured:
I will surely gather all of you, O Jacob;
I will collect the remnant of Israel.
I will bring them together like sheep in a pen,
like a flock in the midst of its pasture —
a noisy throng.
differences.authoritative: I will surely gather all of you, O Jacob; I will collect the remnant of Israel. I will bring them together like sheep in a pen, like a flock in the midst of its pasture—a noisy throng.

differences.structured:
And you, O watchtower of the flock,
O stronghold of the Daughter of Zion —
the former dominion will be restored to you;
sovereignty will come to the Daughter of Jerusalem.”
differences.authoritative: And you, O watchtower of the flock, O stronghold of the Daughter of Zion—the former dominion will be restored to you; sovereignty will come to the Daughter of Jerusalem.”

differences.structured:
But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah,
who are small among the clans of Judah,
out of you will come forth for Me
One to be ruler over Israel—
One whose origins are of old,
from the days of eternity.
differences.authoritative: But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah, who are small among the clans of Judah, out of you will come forth for Me One to be ruler over Israel—One whose origins are of old, from the days of eternity.

differences.structured:
Then my enemy will see
and will be covered with shame —
she who said to me,
“Where is the LORD your God?”
My eyes will see her;
at that time she will be trampled
like mud in the streets.
differences.authoritative: Then my enemy will see and will be covered with shame—she who said to me, “Where is the LORD your God?” My eyes will see her; at that time she will be trampled like mud in the streets.

differences.structured:
The day for rebuilding your walls will come —
the day for extending your boundary.
differences.authoritative: The day for rebuilding your walls will come—the day for extending your boundary.

differences.structured:
Who is a God like You,
who pardons iniquity
and passes over the transgression
of the remnant of His inheritance —
who does not retain His anger forever,
because He delights in loving devotion?
differences.authoritative: Who is a God like You, who pardons iniquity and passes over the transgression of the remnant of His inheritance—who does not retain His anger forever, because He delights in loving devotion?

differences.structured:
The mountains quake before Him,
and the hills melt away;
the earth trembles at His presence—
the world and all its dwellers.
differences.authoritative: The mountains quake before Him, and the hills melt away; the earth trembles at His presence—the world and all its dwellers.

differences.structured:
For they will be entangled as with thorns
and consumed like the drink of a drunkard —
like stubble that is fully dry.
differences.authoritative: For they will be entangled as with thorns and consumed like the drink of a drunkard—like stubble that is fully dry.

differences.structured:
Look to the mountains—
the feet of one who brings good news,
who proclaims peace!
Celebrate your feasts, O Judah;
fulfill your vows.
For the wicked will never again march through you;
they will be utterly cut off.
differences.authoritative: Look to the mountains—the feet of one who brings good news, who proclaims peace! Celebrate your feasts, O Judah; fulfill your vows. For the wicked will never again march through you; they will be utterly cut off.

differences.structured:
Charging horseman,
flashing sword,
shining spear;
heaps of slain,
mounds of corpses,
dead bodies without end—
they stumble over their dead—
differences.authoritative: Charging horseman, flashing sword, shining spear; heaps of slain, mounds of corpses, dead bodies without end—they stumble over their dead—

differences.structured:
Look at your troops —
they are like your women!
The gates of your land
are wide open to your enemies;
fire consumes their bars.
differences.authoritative: Look at your troops—they are like your women! The gates of your land are wide open to your enemies; fire consumes their bars.

differences.structured:
“Look at the nations and observe—
be utterly astounded!
For I am doing a work in your days
that you would never believe
even if someone told you.
differences.authoritative: “Look at the nations and observe—be utterly astounded! For I am doing a work in your days that you would never believe even if someone told you.

differences.structured:
For behold, I am raising up the Chaldeans —
that ruthless and impetuous nation
which marches through the breadth of the earth
to seize dwellings not their own.
differences.authoritative: For behold, I am raising up the Chaldeans—that ruthless and impetuous nation which marches through the breadth of the earth to seize dwellings not their own.

differences.structured:
Look at the proud one; his soul is not upright —
but the righteous will live by faith —
differences.authoritative: Look at the proud one; his soul is not upright—but the righteous will live by faith—

differences.structured:
Because you have plundered many nations,
the remnant of the people will plunder you—
because of your bloodshed against man
and your violence against the land, the city,
and all their dwellers.
differences.authoritative: Because you have plundered many nations, the remnant of the people will plunder you—because of your bloodshed against man and your violence against the land, the city, and all their dwellers.

differences.structured:
What use is an idol,
that a craftsman should carve it —
or an image,
a teacher of lies?
For its maker trusts in his own creation;
he makes idols that cannot speak.
differences.authoritative: What use is an idol, that a craftsman should carve it—or an image, a teacher of lies? For its maker trusts in his own creation; he makes idols that cannot speak.

differences.structured:
“I will stretch out My hand against Judah
and against all who dwell in Jerusalem.
I will cut off from this place every remnant of Baal,
the names of the idolatrous and pagan priests —
differences.authoritative: “I will stretch out My hand against Judah and against all who dwell in Jerusalem. I will cut off from this place every remnant of Baal, the names of the idolatrous and pagan priests—

differences.structured:
The great Day of the LORD is near —
near and coming quickly.
Listen, the Day of the LORD!
Then the cry of the mighty will be bitter.
differences.authoritative: The great Day of the LORD is near—near and coming quickly. Listen, the Day of the LORD! Then the cry of the mighty will be bitter.

differences.structured:
Therefore, as surely as I live,”
declares the LORD of Hosts,
the God of Israel,
“surely Moab will be like Sodom
and the Ammonites like Gomorrah—
a place of weeds and salt pits,
a perpetual wasteland.
The remnant of My people will plunder them;
the remainder of My nation will dispossess them.”
differences.authoritative: Therefore, as surely as I live,” declares the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, “surely Moab will be like Sodom and the Ammonites like Gomorrah—a place of weeds and salt pits, a perpetual wasteland. The remnant of My people will plunder them; the remainder of My nation will dispossess them.”

differences.structured:
Therefore wait for Me,”
declares the LORD,
“until the day
I rise to testify.
For My decision is to gather nations,
to assemble kingdoms,
to pour out upon them My indignation —
all My burning anger.
For all the earth will be consumed
by the fire of My jealousy.
differences.authoritative: Therefore wait for Me,” declares the LORD, “until the day I rise to testify. For My decision is to gather nations, to assemble kingdoms, to pour out upon them My indignation—all My burning anger. For all the earth will be consumed by the fire of My jealousy.

differences.structured: I struck you— all the work of your hands— with blight, mildew, and hail, but you did not turn to Me, declares the LORD.
differences.authoritative: I struck you—all the work of your hands—with blight, mildew, and hail, but you did not turn to Me, declares the LORD.

differences.structured: Consider carefully from this day forward — from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, the day the foundation of the LORD’s temple was laid — consider carefully:
differences.authoritative: Consider carefully from this day forward—from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, the day the foundation of the LORD’s temple was laid—consider carefully:

differences.structured: For this is what the LORD of Hosts says: “After His Glory has sent Me against the nations that have plundered you — for whoever touches you touches the apple of His eye —
differences.authoritative: For this is what the LORD of Hosts says: “After His Glory has sent Me against the nations that have plundered you—for whoever touches you touches the apple of His eye—

differences.structured: And again I lifted up my eyes and saw four chariots coming out from between two mountains — mountains of bronze.
differences.authoritative: And again I lifted up my eyes and saw four chariots coming out from between two mountains—mountains of bronze.

differences.structured: the third white horses, and the fourth dappled horses— all of them strong.
differences.authoritative: the third white horses, and the fourth dappled horses—all of them strong.

differences.structured: “Take an offering from the exiles — from Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah, who have arrived from Babylon — and go that same day to the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah.
differences.authoritative: “Take an offering from the exiles—from Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah, who have arrived from Babylon—and go that same day to the house of Josiah son of Zephaniah.

differences.structured: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Peoples will yet come — the residents of many cities —
differences.authoritative: This is what the LORD of Hosts says: “Peoples will yet come—the residents of many cities—

differences.structured:
This is the burden of the word of the LORD
against the land of Hadrach
and Damascus its resting place—
for the eyes of men
and of all the tribes of Israel
are upon the LORD—
differences.authoritative: This is the burden of the word of the LORD against the land of Hadrach and Damascus its resting place—for the eyes of men and of all the tribes of Israel are upon the LORD—

differences.structured: And the LORD said to me, “Throw it to the potter”— this magnificent price at which they valued me. So I took the thirty pieces of silver and threw them to the potter in the house of the LORD.
differences.authoritative: And the LORD said to me, “Throw it to the potter”—this magnificent price at which they valued me. So I took the thirty pieces of silver and threw them to the potter in the house of the LORD.

differences.structured: and all the remaining clans and their wives.’’
differences.authoritative: and all the remaining clans and their wives.
differences.engineeringDecision: extra closing-quote string in USJ; retain TXT

differences.structured: On that day the LORD will become King over all the earth— the LORD alone, and His name alone.
differences.authoritative: On that day the LORD will become King over all the earth—the LORD alone, and His name alone.

differences.structured: Judah will also fight at Jerusalem, and the wealth of all the surrounding nations will be collected — gold, silver, and apparel in great abundance.
differences.authoritative: Judah will also fight at Jerusalem, and the wealth of all the surrounding nations will be collected—gold, silver, and apparel in great abundance.

differences.structured: You will see this with your own eyes, and you yourselves will say, ‘The LORD is great — even beyond the borders of Israel.’”
differences.authoritative: You will see this with your own eyes, and you yourselves will say, ‘The LORD is great—even beyond the borders of Israel.’”

differences.structured: “But cursed is the deceiver who has an acceptable male in his flock and vows to give it, but sacrifices a defective animal to the Lord. For I am a great King,” says the LORD of Hosts, “and My name is to be feared among the nations.’’
differences.authoritative: “But cursed is the deceiver who has an acceptable male in his flock and vows to give it, but sacrifices a defective animal to the Lord. For I am a great King,” says the LORD of Hosts, “and My name is to be feared among the nations.
differences.engineeringDecision: extra closing-quote string in USJ; retain TXT

differences.structured: As for the man who does this, may the LORD cut off from the tents of Jacob everyone who is awake and aware — even if he brings an offering to the LORD of Hosts.
differences.authoritative: As for the man who does this, may the LORD cut off from the tents of Jacob everyone who is awake and aware—even if he brings an offering to the LORD of Hosts.

differences.structured: “Behold, I will send My messenger, who will prepare the way before Me. Then the Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to His temple — the Messenger of the covenant, in whom you delight — see, He is coming,” says the LORD of Hosts.
differences.authoritative: “Behold, I will send My messenger, who will prepare the way before Me. Then the Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to His temple—the Messenger of the covenant, in whom you delight—see, He is coming,” says the LORD of Hosts.

differences.structured: You are cursed with a curse, yet you— the whole nation— are still robbing Me.
differences.authoritative: You are cursed with a curse, yet you—the whole nation—are still robbing Me.
